pages.text: A $(thing)catena$() is the chain of soils down a hillside. Water, dissolved minerals and fine particles all move downhill, so position on the slope decides the soil.

$(li)$(thing)Summit:$() stable, moderately deep, well drained.$(li)$(thing)Shoulder:$() the most eroded: thin, sandy, low in organic matter.$(li)$(thing)Backslope:$() steep and thin.$(li)$(thing)Footslope:$() deeper, receives soil from above.
$(li)$(thing)Depression:$() a hollow with no outlet. Wet, clayey and gleyed; in cold climates it fills with peat.$(li)$(thing)Floodplain:$() silty river sediment over a shallow water table.
The parent material (wind-blown loess, glacial till, river alluvium, lake clay, dune sand) sets the starting texture.
Use $(thing)/tilth catena$() anywhere to see the slope, curvature, relief, hillslope position and the soil profile the land implies. Worldgen builds every new chunk this way.
